n: After two days and nights, the family prepares to place Lamoni’s body in a tomb.

f.g: A tomb, often cut from rock.

n: The queen, having heard of Ammon’s fame, sends for him.
Ammon comes and asks how he can help.

f.w: what she would that he should do
f.g: Ammon remains the humble servant.

n: The queen has heard from the servants that Ammon is a prophet of a holy God with power to do mighty works.

f.w: a prophet of a holy God
f.g: She has already begun to believe through others’ testimony.

n: She asks him to see her husband. Some say he is dead and decaying; she senses he is not.

f.w: to me he doth not stink
f.g: An early sign of the queen’s spiritual sensitivity.

n: This was what Ammon wanted. He knew Lamoni was under God’s power — the veil of unbelief lifted, his mind filled with God’s marvelous light, his body overcome as he was “carried away in God.”

f.g: His physical body and ordinary strength.

n: Ammon goes in and sees the king is not dead.

f.g: Ammon’s spiritual discernment confirms it.

n: He tells the queen: he is not dead, but sleeps in God, and will rise tomorrow. Do not bury him.

f.w: He is not dead, but he sleepeth

n: Ammon asks if she believes. She has only his word and the servants’, yet she believes.
Ammon praises her faith as greater than any among the Nephites — a remarkable tribute to a Lamanite woman.

f.w: there has not been such great faith

n: She watches over her husband all night until the appointed time.

f.g: Faith expressed through patient waiting.

n: Lamoni rises as promised, reaches for his wife, and blesses God and her.

f.w: Blessed be the name of God

n: Lamoni testifies he has seen his Redeemer, who will be born of a woman and redeem all who believe. Overwhelmed with joy, he and the queen both sink down, overpowered by the Spirit.
Seeing the Spirit poured out on the Lamanites in answer to his prayers, Ammon kneels in thanksgiving and is also overcome with joy. All three lie on the ground.
The servants who had testified of Ammon’s power now cry to God in fear.

f.g: Reverent awe.

n: They pray mightily until all fall — except Abish, a Lamanite woman who had secretly been converted years earlier through her father’s remarkable vision.

f.g: One of the few women named in the Book of Mormon.

f.w: a remarkable vision of her father
f.g: No further detail is given.

n: Abish, who had never revealed her faith, recognizes God’s power and runs house to house to gather witnesses, hoping the scene will lead people to believe.

f.g: She had kept her faith quietly until the right moment came.

n: A crowd gathers and is astonished to see the king, queen, and servants lying as if dead — and a Nephite among them.

f.g: An enemy in their eyes, deepening their suspicion.

n: Some blame the Nephite’s presence for the calamity.

f.g: They read the scene as a curse.

n: Others say the king brought it on himself by executing his servants.
Men from the Sebus incident, angry about their slain companions, add to the uproar.
One whose brother Ammon had killed raises his sword to strike Ammon — and falls dead.
Mormon explains: the Lord had promised Mosiah to spare his son, according to Mosiah’s faith.
Seeing this, the crowd is afraid to touch Ammon or anyone fallen, and wonders what power is at work.

f.w: they durst not put forth their hands
f.g: They dared not.

n: Some say Ammon is the Great Spirit; others, that he was sent by the Great Spirit.
Others call him a monster sent to torment them.

f.g: Fear twists their interpretation.

n: Some reason that the Great Spirit has always protected the Nephites and is now punishing the Lamanites.

f.w: who had ever delivered them out of their hands
f.g: An insight closer to the truth than they realized.

n: The argument grows sharp. Abish returns, sees the contention, and weeps.

f.g: Her hope to bring belief seems to be turning into conflict.

n: Abish takes the queen’s hand; the queen rises and cries out, praising Jesus for saving her from hell and pleading for mercy on her people.

f.g: Among the first recorded Lamanite expressions of faith in Jesus by name.

n: Filled with joy, the queen speaks words no one understands, then raises the king by the hand.

f.w: speaking many words which were not understood
f.g: Likely the gift of tongues.

n: Lamoni rebukes the arguing crowd and teaches what Ammon taught him. Those who listen are converted.

f.w: began to rebuke them, and to teach them
f.g: The new convert immediately becomes a teacher.

n: Many refuse to listen and leave.
Ammon and the servants rise and teach as well, all testifying that their hearts have changed and they no longer desire evil.

f.w: they had no more desire to do evil

n: Many say they have seen and spoken with angels who taught them about God’s righteousness.
Many believe and are baptized, become righteous, and establish a church.
So begins the Lord’s work among the Lamanites. His arm reaches out to all who repent and believe.

f.w: his arm is extended to all people
